entries: Push and pull: a push moves the box away across the table and a pull drags it back closer - both are forces, and forces change how things move.
slots.label: Push and pull
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Friction slows things down: the block slides down the slope while the rough surface rubs against it, and the friction arrow pushes back against the slide.
slots.label: Friction slows things down
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Opposite poles attract: every magnet has a north pole and a south pole, and when S faces N the magnets pull together and snap with a click.
slots.label: Opposite poles attract
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Watch out: a magnet does not attract every metal: turn the magnet so N faces N and the magnets repel, and remember the magnet only pulls iron and a few metals, ignoring most things.
slots.label: Watch out
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: A force that moves something away from you: kicking a ball and shoving a box across a table are pushes.
slots.label: Push
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A force that brings something closer to you: dragging a box towards you and reeling in a kite are pulls.
slots.label: Pull
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The rubbing force between surfaces that slide against each other: it pushes back against the sliding and slows things down.
slots.label: Friction
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The two ends of a magnet, marked N and S: opposite poles attract and like poles repel.
slots.label: Poles
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.
